statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-123872 is a client-certificate authentication bypass in Node.js TLS: on a server that applies different client-certificate policies per server name, a client that authenticated for one name can switch to another name during TLS 1.2 renegotiation and carry its authentication to a host with a stricter policy. The November 2026 security advisory lists the 22.x, 24.x and 26.x lines as affected (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/november-2026-security-releases). Node.js fixed 24.x in 24.22.3 (https://github.com/nodejs/node/releases/tag/v24.22.3) with three commits that carry this CVE id and are not in 24.22.2: https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/981d2defc6 (tls: don't allow renegotiation or HRR to change SNI), https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/799abe55cb (tls: don't allow TLS resumption to change SNI) and https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/599ca08e28 (tls: disable resumption for mTLS with no session id context). We read the version string from the node binary in every published nodejs-24 package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository (24.13.0-r0 to the current 24.22.3-r0, x86_64 and aarch64); each matches its package version, so builds below 24.22.3-r0 ship Node.js 24.22.2 or older and 24.22.3-r0, the current build, ships 24.22.3. The node binary of 24.22.3-r0 contains the error message the first of these commits adds ('ClientHello asked for server name ..., connection pinned to ...'), on both architectures, and the 24.22.2-r0 binary does not. The range ends at 24.22.3-r0, the first build with the fix.
